$\frac{3}{4} \div \frac{9}{16} \times \frac{3}{8} - \frac{1}{3} = ?$

solution.trap: $3\frac{2}{9}$ multiplies $\frac{9}{16} \times \frac{3}{8}$ first ($\frac{3}{4} \div \frac{27}{128} = \frac{32}{9}$). ÷ and × run left to right. $\frac{1}{2}$ forgets to subtract $\frac{1}{3}$.

solution.trap: **1** forgets the $\frac{2}{3} \text{ of }$ in front of the bracket ($\frac{11}{4} \times ? = \frac{11}{4}$).

solution.trap: **45** takes $13^{2}$ as 179; $13^{2} = 169$. Also check $14^{3} = 2744$ exactly, so the cube root is 14.

solution.trap: Stopping at $\sqrt{?} = 22$ and not squaring is the classic slip. **441** ($21^{2}$) comes from taking $\sqrt{1089}$ as 34; $33^{2} = 1089$.
